sentences.1: The atoms, as their own weight bears them down plumb through the void, at scarce determined times, in scarce determined places, from their course decline a little; call it, so to speak, mere changed trend.
sentences.2: For were it not their wont thuswise to swerve, down would not they fall, each one, like drops of rain, through the unbottomed void; and then collisions ne'er could be nor blows among the primal elements; and thus Nature would never have created aught.
sentences.3: But, if perchance be any that believe the heavier bodies, as more swiftly borne plumb down the void, are able from above to strike the lighter, thus engendering blows able to cause those procreant motions, far from highways of true reason they retire.
sentences.4: For whatsoever through the waters fall, or through thin air, must quicken their descent, each after its weight; on this account, because both bulk of water and the subtle air by no means can retard each thing alike, but give more quick before the heavier weight.
sentences.5: But contrariwise the empty void cannot, on any side, at any time, to aught oppose resistance, but will ever yield, true to its bent of nature.
sentences.6: Wherefore all, with equal speed, though equal not in weight, must rush, borne downward through the still inane.
sentences.7: Thus ne'er at all have heavier from above been swift to strike the lighter, gendering strokes able to cause those procreant motions.
